title: Choose the BugReceipt prototype structure
question: All three preserve the Evidence Desk identity and the Report → Evidence → Export check sequence. Choose the composition that should become the interactive prototype.

options.label: Export Ledger
options.thesis: A wide verification desk where the active task fills the canvas and an export ledger accumulates along the bottom edge.
options.viewport: A three-step rail spans the top, the evidence workspace dominates the center, and a persistent bottom ledger previews exactly what will leave the device.
options.risk: The bottom ledger can compete with dense evidence unless it collapses intelligently.

options.label: Evidence Cockpit
options.thesis: A focused central evidence canvas flanked by report context and a live bundle manifest.
options.viewport: A compact stage header sits above three columns: report synopsis, active evidence, and a receipt-like manifest with readiness and redaction totals.
options.risk: Three columns may feel compressed at ordinary laptop widths and require disciplined collapse behavior.

options.label: Receipt Spine
options.thesis: A continuous left-hand receipt spine makes every stage, count, warning, and completion state visible without competing with the active task.
options.viewport: A narrow evidence-receipt rail anchors the left; the active stage uses the rest of the screen with a compact contextual action bar and no permanent export controls.
options.risk: The spine must remain legible without becoming another navigation sidebar.
